description: Bug and issue register for the SIH 2026 nowcasting system. Rendered live in the dashboard's Diagnostics panel.

issues.title: Model trained on Gaussian noise, scored on physical units
issues.detail: generate_synthetic_training_data drew X from np.random.randn, so every tree split sat in roughly [-3, 3]. Inference fed real values such as pressure 1013 hPa and brightness temperature 250 K, so every real sample fell off the same end of every split and the output collapsed to a near-constant probability.
issues.impact: The dashboard's probability gauge was effectively a constant. It did not respond to the imagery.
issues.fix: Synthetic features are now drawn on their true physical scales, a temporal train/test split is enforced, and the model card records training_data='synthetic' so every surface labels the output as a demonstration.

issues.title: Silent feature column-order mismatch
issues.detail: build_feature_vector returned features sorted alphabetically; train_and_save_model assigned names in a different hand-written order; the saved model carried no feature_names at all. XGBoost silently accepted any column order.
issues.impact: Wrong values were fed into the wrong trees with no error raised.
issues.fix: FeatureContract persists the ordered names plus the training distribution. align() looks features up BY NAME, and load_model() refuses any model saved without a contract.

issues.title: No radar, lightning or NWP data despite being named in the problem statement
issues.detail: PS 26072 requires 'multiple radars, satellite, lightning and model data'. The original implemented only simulated satellite imagery plus a point weather API.
issues.impact: Three of the four required data legs were absent; radar and lightning appeared only in the pitch documents.
issues.fix: utils/datasources/ adds IMD DWR multi-radar composites, lightning network adapters with a local-archive path, and live NWP convective parameters. Each returns explicit provenance.

issues.title: Simulated imagery presented as real observations
issues.detail: generate_sample_satellite_images produced random blobs with np.random.seed(42); the dashboard captioned them 'Latest IR Image'. fetch_mosdac_data never fetched anything - it wrote a config file, printed instructions and returned an empty list.
issues.impact: A judge would reasonably have believed they were looking at live INSAT data.
issues.fix: Every source returns a SourceStatus (live / cached / stale / simulated / unavailable / needs_credentials). Simulated data is labelled in the UI and cannot be mistaken for an observation. Live INSAT imagery now works via the public MOSDAC gallery endpoint.

issues.title: No verification metrics; accuracy quoted on training data
issues.detail: Documentation claimed '99%+ accuracy on synthetic data'. That was training-set accuracy on random noise. No train/test split, no POD/FAR/CSI, no ROC - the metrics IMD and WMO actually use for rare-event verification.
issues.impact: The headline claim would not survive the first question from a domain expert.
issues.fix: utils/metrics.py implements the full 2x2 contingency table (POD, FAR, CSI, BIAS, HSS, PSS), Brier score, Brier skill score, ROC and reliability curves, plus skill relative to a persistence baseline.

issues.title: Report generator crashes on any missing feature
issues.detail: generate_detailed_report used f-strings of the form {features.get('x', 'N/A'):.2f}. When the key was absent this evaluates format('N/A', '.2f'), which raises ValueError rather than printing 'N/A'.
issues.impact: The detailed report crashed instead of degrading gracefully.
issues.fix: All numeric formatting goes through _fmt(), which type-checks before applying a format spec.

issues.title: Physical thresholds applied to 8-bit display values
issues.detail: Convective detection used 'img < 150' against raw PNG pixel values. Real INSAT L1B products carry brightness temperature in Kelvin, and different browse products use different display stretches.
issues.impact: The physics narrative would not survive contact with real satellite data.
issues.fix: utils/calibration.py converts counts to Kelvin once at ingestion. All thresholds are now stated in Kelvin (241 K anvil, 221 K deep convection, 205 K overshooting top).

issues.title: Lead time silently wrong by a factor of two
issues.detail: create_nowcast_sequence advected by lead_time_steps=1..6 and the comment claimed '6 hours ahead (assuming 1hr steps)'. INSAT imagery arrives every 30 minutes, so six steps is three hours, not six.
issues.impact: Every nowcast frame was labelled with double its true lead time.
issues.fix: nowcast_sequence takes lead times in HOURS and converts using the actual frame interval.

issues.title: use_label_encoder removed in XGBoost 2.0
issues.detail: XGBClassifier(use_label_encoder=False) while requirements.txt pinned xgboost>=2.0.0, where the parameter no longer exists. Installed version here is 3.2.0.
issues.impact: Training would warn or fail on any modern XGBoost.
issues.fix: Parameter removed; eval_metric switched to 'aucpr', which is the appropriate metric for a rare event.

issues.title: Feature importance chart never rendered
issues.detail: The chart was guarded by results.get('predictor'), but run_prediction in app.py never placed 'predictor' in its return dict. The branch was permanently dead and failed silently.
issues.impact: A headline explainability feature was invisible with no error shown.
issues.fix: The merged app returns the predictor and renders grouped feature importance.

issues.title: LLM alert path unreachable from the main app
issues.detail: app.py called generate_template_alert directly, so generate_alert - and therefore the LLM - was never invoked regardless of the configured key. The Groq model id was also 'groq/compound', which is not a chat model and returned HTTP 403 (recorded in the committed api_test_results.json).
issues.impact: The advertised LLM alerting never ran.
issues.fix: generate_alert is the single entry point and falls back to templates internally. Model id defaults to llama-3.3-70b-versatile and is configurable via GROQ_MODEL.

issues.title: Cloud simulator produced incoherent, untrackable motion
issues.detail: Cell masks used np.ogrid[-cx:256-cx, -cy:256-cy], placing cx on the row axis and cy on the column axis - the coordinates were swapped. Noise was re-added inside the per-cell loop, compounding with each cell. Motion came from np.roll, which wraps at the edges.
issues.impact: No optical-flow method could track the result coherently, so the flow features were noise.
issues.fix: The simulator now models advection with a common steering flow, cell life cycles that cool then warm, and downshear anvil spreading.

issues.title: Circular mean computed as an arithmetic mean
issues.detail: flow_direction_mean averaged degrees arithmetically. The mean of 359 deg and 1 deg is 180 deg by that method - the exact opposite of the true direction.
issues.impact: The reported storm bearing could be inverted.
issues.fix: Direction now uses the circular mean via atan2 of summed sine and cosine components, with circular standard deviation.

issues.title: Advection applied the flow field with the wrong sign
issues.detail: advect_image built its remap grid as coordinate + flow. cv2.remap samples the SOURCE location for each destination pixel, so forward advection requires coordinate - flow. The original moved cloud features backwards along their motion vector.
issues.impact: Nowcast frames advected storms in the reverse direction.
issues.fix: The remap grid now subtracts the flow, and the sign convention is documented in the docstring.

issues.title: Deprecated Streamlit and Python APIs
issues.detail: st.image(use_column_width=True) is removed in current Streamlit (1.63 installed here), and datetime.utcnow() is deprecated from Python 3.12.
issues.impact: Deprecation warnings now, breakage on the next release.
issues.fix: Switched to use_container_width and timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc).

issues.title: Two near-duplicate dashboards with no stated entry point
issues.detail: About 200 lines of pipeline code were copy-pasted between the two files, and they had diverged - app_enhanced.py returned the predictor while app.py did not.
issues.impact: Fixes applied to one file silently missed the other.
issues.fix: Merged into a single app.py.

issues.title: Return type contradicted the annotation
issues.detail: build_feature_vector was annotated '-> np.ndarray' but returned a (vector, names) tuple.
issues.impact: Misleading to callers and to type checkers.
issues.fix: build_features returns a Dict[str, float] and is annotated accordingly.

issues.title: Convergence diluted by clear-air pixels
issues.detail: Convergence was averaged over the entire scene, including clear air where it carries no convective meaning.
issues.impact: The one genuinely predictive flow feature was buried in noise.
issues.fix: Added convergence_in_cold_cloud, restricted to pixels beneath cold cloud tops where new cells actually develop.

issues.title: Unused parameter in the flow feature extractor
issues.detail: extract_flow_features(flow, img) never used img.
issues.impact: Dead parameter implying a capability that was not there.
issues.fix: The brightness-temperature field is now genuinely used, to mask convergence to cold cloud.

issues.title: Wrong API key format in the example environment file
issues.detail: GROQ_API_KEY was shown as 'groq_xxx...'. Real Groq keys begin with 'gsk_'.
issues.impact: Minor, but it sends a new contributor looking for the wrong thing.
issues.fix: Corrected, and MOSDAC_BROWSE_URL plus the lightning network variables documented.

issues.title: int16 overflow made radar decode terrain as 40 dBZ echo
issues.detail: Nearest-colour matching computed squared RGB distances in int16. A squared channel difference reaches 255^2 = 65025 and the three-channel sum reaches 195075, both far beyond the int16 maximum of 32767, so the arithmetic wrapped around. Genuinely distant colours scored as near matches: the green terrain basemap (100,173,64) wrapped to a small distance and decoded as a 40 dBZ echo.
issues.impact: Radar reported ~50% echo coverage and a pinned 61 dBZ maximum on every scan, including clear skies. Caught by cross-checking decoded coverage against the visible image.
issues.fix: Distances are computed in int32. Decoded coverage for Delhi fell from 49.8% to 1.65%, Goa to 0.03% (clear), and Jot correctly shows a 58 dBZ convective core. Verified against a pixel overlay of the source image.

issues.title: Radar legend and basemap decoded as reflectivity
issues.detail: IMD MAX_Z products embed vertical cross-section panels, a station info box and a printed colour-scale legend, all drawn in the same palette as the echoes. Decoding the whole frame counted the legend's top swatch as a 60+ dBZ core on every fetch.
issues.impact: Peak reflectivity was pinned at the palette maximum regardless of actual weather.
issues.fix: detect_scan_area locates the circular PPI disc from the green terrain basemap and intersects it with the basemap bounding box, excluding panels and legend. The palette is now READ FROM the legend printed in each image rather than hardcoded, so it adapts per station.

issues.title: ROC AUC understated by integrating a sampled curve
issues.detail: AUC was computed by trapezoidal integration of the ROC curve sampled on a 51-point threshold grid. Many thresholds share the same false-alarm rate, so once the points were sorted by x the trapezoid rule integrated straight through the vertical segment at x=0 and discarded its area. Perfectly separable data scored 0.833 instead of 1.0.
issues.impact: Every reported AUC was biased low, which would have understated the model in the verification panel and in the report.
issues.fix: Replaced with the exact Mann-Whitney rank identity (AUC = probability a random positive outranks a random negative), with average ranks for ties. Caught by test_auc_of_perfect_separation_is_one.

issues.title: No observed training labels yet
issues.detail: The model is still fitted to synthetic data. Real skill requires training against observed lightning strikes as labels, over at least one storm season.
issues.impact: Until this is done the system demonstrates a working pipeline, not a skilful forecast. Every surface says so.
issues.next_step: Drop an IITM/ENTLN lightning export into data/lightning/ as CSV (time,lat,lon), collect INSAT frames over a season, then run scripts/train_real.py. utils.datasources.lightning.build_labels already implements the forward-looking event definition.

issues.title: Only 3 of 36 DWR sites publish public products
issues.detail: Probing mausam.imd.gov.in found live products for Delhi, Goa and Jot only. The remaining stations either use different URL slugs or are not published publicly.
issues.impact: The multi-radar composite usually has one contributing radar, not several.
issues.next_step: Institutional access to IMD Level-II volumes would resolve this. The network probe in utils.datasources.radar.network_status reports live status honestly in the meantime.

issues.title: Satellite brightness temperature is uncalibrated
issues.detail: The public MOSDAC gallery serves rendered 8-bit JPEGs. Kelvin is recovered by inverting an assumed linear display stretch (180-320 K), which is an approximation.
issues.impact: Absolute cloud-top temperatures carry systematic error; relative structure and cooling rates are still usable.
issues.next_step: Register for a free MOSDAC account and use the L1B NetCDF Order API, which carries true calibrated Kelvin.

issues.title: Cloud motion needs two INSAT scans to become available
issues.detail: The public gallery serves only the newest scan per product, so a motion estimate requires frames accumulated across runs. The rolling buffer collects them, deduplicated by content hash.
issues.impact: On a cold start, motion features are zero and the UI says so.
issues.next_step: Run the collector (scripts/collect_frames.py) on a 30-minute schedule to keep the buffer warm ahead of a demonstration.

issues.title: Full-disk to India crop was not georeferenced
issues.detail: The Indian region is cut from the full disk using fixed pixel fractions rather than the L1B geolocation grid, so features are not precisely georeferenced to the selected city.
issues.impact: Satellite features describe the broad Indian region rather than the specific point.
issues.fix: Replaced the fixed pixel fractions with a proper geostationary (GEOS) reprojection onto EPSG:4326. Validated against the graticule burned into the source product: the 10, 20 and 30 degree parallels land within 0.03-0.07 degrees. Satellite features are now extracted for a real bounding box and the ISRO Bhuvan boundary registers with the coastline.

issues.title: Earth-disk detection corrupted by the MOSDAC title bar
issues.detail: MOSDAC browse products carry a title bar, a greyscale colour wedge and ISRO/MOSDAC logos across the top, all drawn in bright white. Detecting the Earth disk by thresholding and taking a bounding box included that furniture, pulling the fitted centre up by ~140 px and inflating the radius by ~60 px.
issues.impact: Every georeferenced coordinate was wrong by hundreds of kilometres, so boundary overlays and per-city feature extraction were both misregistered.
issues.fix: The disk is isolated as the largest connected component, then refined with a least-squares circle fit to the limb. Latitude error against the graticule burned into the source fell from 0.17-0.45 degrees to 0.03-0.07 degrees, which is sub-pixel at INSAT's 4 km resolution.

issues.title: Geostationary projection flipped the image vertically
issues.detail: The scan angle was computed as arcsin(-r3/rn), following the raw CGMS listing, which assumes a south-first scan. INSAT browse images are stored north-up, so northern latitudes mapped to LARGER row indices and the reprojection sampled the southern hemisphere.
issues.impact: The 'Indian region' crop actually returned southern Indian Ocean. It went unnoticed at first because the cyan boundary overlay drawn on top still looked like India; the giveaway was the source graticule labels reading -30 and -50.
issues.fix: Sign corrected in both the forward and inverse projection, with a regression test asserting that row indices increase monotonically southward.

issues.title: Satellite misidentified as INSAT-3D
issues.detail: The 3SIMG_ product prefix was labelled INSAT-3D throughout. The header printed inside the image itself reads 'INSAT-3DS IMG, Thermal Infrared1 Count @ 10.78 um', so the feed is INSAT-3DS.
issues.impact: Every UI label, citation and report named the wrong spacecraft - the kind of detail a domain panel notices immediately.
issues.fix: Channels relabelled INSAT-3DS, and each now carries its sub-satellite longitude (82 E for 3DS, 74 E for 3DR) so the projection is correct per satellite.

issues.title: Frame buffer mixed georeferenced and un-georeferenced frames
issues.detail: Switching the crop to a real geostationary reprojection changed the pixel geometry, but frames cached under the old fixed-fraction crop remained in the rolling buffer.
issues.impact: Optical flow would have compared two different projections and reported large spurious cloud motion.
issues.fix: Buffer cleared as part of the change. Frames are keyed by content hash, so the buffer refills cleanly from the next scan.

issues.title: Palette rename could blank the entire app at import time
issues.found: frontend/landing.py:58 (reported from a Streamlit Cloud deployment)
issues.detail: The landing page's APPROACH constant resolved theme colours at MODULE level (theme.BLUE). That runs during import, so any mismatch between the page and the palette raised AttributeError before Streamlit rendered anything at all. A deployment served a stale theme module alongside the new landing page and the whole dashboard showed a traceback instead of the app.
issues.impact: Total outage from a cosmetic value. The repository code was self-consistent; only the deployed container was stale, but the failure mode was fatal rather than degraded.
issues.fix: Presentation constants now hold SEMANTIC colour names resolved at render time by _tint(), which falls back to a literal. A palette gap now costs one swatch instead of the application. Modules inside the frontend package also import theme relatively, so no same-named package on sys.path can shadow it. Three regression tests were added: every theme reference in app.py, landing.py and globe.py must resolve; presentation constants must not hold resolved colours; and the landing page must render against a deliberately stale palette.

issues.title: Primary button label invisible against its filled background
issues.detail: The stylesheet contained a blanket `section[data-testid="stSidebar"] *` rule setting every descendant to muted ink. Streamlit wraps a button's label in an inner element, and that broad descendant selector won on the inner node - the primary button rule only targets the <button> itself, so its white colour never reached the label. The Run nowcast button rendered as a solid blue block with no readable text.
issues.impact: The main call to action in the sidebar was unreadable. A judge opening the app would not know how to start a nowcast.
issues.fix: The sidebar rule is now scoped to specific elements instead of using a universal selector, and button label colour is set on the button AND on every descendant for both primary and secondary variants. Comments in the stylesheet record why, since the universal selector is an easy thing to reintroduce.

issues.title: Sequential network probes stalled the whole application
issues.detail: Both functions probed radar sites one at a time, with retries and a long timeout each. network_status took 97 seconds to report that 0 of 12 sites were live, and fetch_radar_mosaic took over three minutes for six unreachable stations. Streamlit executes every tab body on every rerun, so this ran on each interaction.
issues.impact: The dashboard appeared frozen whenever IMD was unreachable, which is often. On a hosted deployment it looked exactly like a failed or stale deploy - the app simply never finished rendering. This was almost certainly why updates appeared not to be taking effect.
issues.fix: Both are now issued concurrently with a single attempt, a short per-request timeout and a hard overall deadline. network_status fell from 97 s to 4.3 s for 12 sites and 12.1 s for all 36; the mosaic fell from over 180 s to 12.3 s. A liveness probe should fail fast, because an unreachable site is itself the answer.

issues.title: Duplicated descriptions and a broken word in the metric cards
issues.detail: Converting the tab headings to the new band component left the original st.caption calls in place, so three sections printed the same sentence twice. Separately, the metric value was a fixed 2 rem, so a long single word broke mid-word in a narrow column and MODERATE rendered as 'MODER ATE'.
issues.impact: Cosmetic, but both are the kind of detail an evaluator notices immediately.
issues.fix: The three duplicated captions were removed. Metric values now scale with the column via clamp() and never break inside a word.

issues.title: Hero animation froze on its first frame when RAF was throttled
issues.detail: The scene advanced time by accumulating requestAnimationFrame deltas. When the component is embedded in an iframe, or the window is not foregrounded, RAF can be throttled to a standstill - the clock then stops permanently and the sky freezes on a single static frame. Measured directly: the exposed scene clock sat at exactly 0.000 s across eighteen seconds. The same throttling stalled the JavaScript tween library, leaving the headline at opacity 0, which would have shipped as a blank hero.
issues.impact: The centrepiece of the landing page would have been a still image with no text on it.
issues.fix: Scene time is now read from the wall clock rather than accumulated from frame deltas, so a stalled loop resumes at the correct point instead of freezing. A timer backstop drives a draw whenever RAF has not run for 200 ms. Text reveals were moved to CSS keyframes, which are compositor-driven and complete regardless. Verified after the fix: the clock advances 6.4 to 14.4 to 21.4 s and a lightning strike was captured mid-flash at 0.745.

issues.title: Variable shadowed the render function and killed the scene
issues.detail: The viewport-sizing code declared `var frame = window.frameElement`, which shadowed the hoisted `frame()` render function. The animation loop then called an iframe element and threw TypeError: frame is not a function on every tick - hundreds of identical errors and a scene that never drew.
issues.impact: The globe was invisible; the landing page showed an empty gradient.
issues.fix: Renamed the element reference to hostFrame. Caught by reading the component's console rather than assuming the blank canvas was a shader problem.

issues.title: Pinned canvas pushed all content below the fold
issues.detail: The globe layer used position: sticky, which still occupies its own layout height. With the layer a full viewport tall, the first content panel started one screen down: scrollHeight measured 5544 for six panels in a 792 px frame, exactly one panel too many. No panel was ever in view at rest, so nothing revealed.
issues.impact: The landing page opened on a globe with no words on it.
issues.fix: Inside this iframe the frame is the viewport, so the layer is position: fixed - pinned correctly and costing no layout height.

issues.title: IntersectionObserver never fired for panel reveals
issues.detail: Reveals were delegated to an IntersectionObserver rooted on the internal scroll container. It never fired inside the embedded frame, leaving every panel at opacity 0 with the copy invisible.
issues.impact: All landing copy would have been blank while the scene animated behind it.
issues.fix: Reveal is computed from the panel rectangle in the scroll handler. A few lines, deterministic, and it cannot silently do nothing. The threshold also treats anything scrolled past as revealed, so a fast scroll cannot strand a panel.

issues.title: Leaving immersive mode raised a Streamlit widget-state error
issues.detail: The exit button assigned to st.session_state.immersive, but that key is bound to the sidebar toggle, which is created earlier in the script. Streamlit raises StreamlitWidgetAlreadyInstantiatedError on any write to a widget-bound key after that widget exists, so pressing the button replaced the page with a traceback.
issues.impact: There was no way back out of immersive mode without restarting.
issues.fix: The button records an intent, and the intent is consumed at the top of the next run before the toggle is instantiated - the point at which the write is legal.
